session.title: Vice-President, Union Subjects and the Close of Volume II

primarySource.publisher: Parliament Digital Library, Lok Sabha Secretariat

transcriptReference.publisher: Constitution of India / Centre for Law and Policy Research

speakers.name: Dr. Rajendra Prasad
speakers.positionSummary: Declares H. C. Mookherjee elected Vice-President, manages two committee resolutions, rules on adjournment procedure and closes Volume II with the Lahiri privilege question still under consideration.

speakers.name: B. Pattabhi Sitaramayya
speakers.positionSummary: Creates a three-member committee to recommend the order of future constitution-making business.

speakers.name: B. Gopala Reddy
speakers.positionSummary: Seconds Pattabhi Sitaramayya's Business Committee resolution.

speakers.name: Satyanarayan Sinha
speakers.positionSummary: Moves the Business Committee quorum amendment, moves Munshi's amendments to the Union-subject committee and later moves adjournment of the preliminary meeting to April.

speakers.name: C. Rajagopalachari
speakers.positionSummary: Argues that the Cabinet Mission framework leaves correlation problems requiring a select committee to work out the scope and interconnection of Union subjects before detailed constitution framing.

speakers.name: C. E. Gibbon
speakers.positionSummary: Questions whether amendments can be anticipated before they are formally moved and whether another member may move Munshi's amendments in his absence.

speakers.name: P. R. Thakur
speakers.positionSummary: Asks the Union-subject committee to consider national responsibilities for communal peace and famine prevention, drawing on Bengal's experience.

speakers.name: Jaipal Singh
speakers.positionSummary: Challenges a committee list he sees as uniform rather than inclusive and asks why tribal areas and figures such as Jayakar, Ambedkar and Deshmukh are absent.

speakers.name: Sardar Harnam Singh
speakers.positionSummary: Argues that this technical committee should be chosen for expertise rather than communal or tribal representation.

speakers.name: N. G. Ranga
speakers.positionSummary: Suggests that one named member withdraw so B. R. Ambedkar can be included in the Union-subject committee.

speakers.name: Unnamed Member
speakers.positionSummary: Raises short procedural questions not attributed by name in the printed record.

speakers.name: K. Santhanam
speakers.positionSummary: Argues that consent to a long adjournment should be tied to a particular future date rather than leave the next sitting indefinite.

speakers.name: Mohan Lal Saksena
speakers.positionSummary: Seconds the motion to adjourn the preliminary meeting to a date in April fixed by the President.

speakers.name: Seth Govind Das
speakers.positionSummary: Opposes binding the Assembly to a fixed April date or a promise of no further adjournment, arguing that conditions may change.

speakers.name: H. V. Kamath
speakers.positionSummary: Moves to prevent any further adjournment of the preliminary meeting beyond April, then withdraws after the mover's reply; later raises Somnath Lahiri's privilege complaint.

speakers.name: N. Gopalaswami Ayyangar
speakers.positionSummary: Supports Santhanam's interpretation that Rule 21 obliges the President to fix a date, even when the House consents to a long adjournment.

speakers.name: Several Members
speakers.positionSummary: Collective responses recorded by the transcript during the adjournment exchange.

speakers.name: Jerome D'Souza
speakers.positionSummary: Congratulates H. C. Mookherjee and stresses his cross-community esteem and educational record.

speakers.name: Sri Biswanath Das
speakers.positionSummary: Treats Mookherjee's election as evidence that minorities need not fear the majority and as an honour to Bengal and minority communities.

speakers.name: H. J. Khandekar
speakers.positionSummary: Offers congratulations on behalf of the Scheduled Caste community he represents.

speakers.name: Joseph Alban D'Souza
speakers.positionSummary: Connects Mookherjee's election to Indian Christian participation and to the community's representation on the Advisory Committee.

speakers.name: H. C. Mookherjee
speakers.positionSummary: Responds to his election by narrating his move from communal politics to Indian nationalism and promising to remember the poor masses rather than act as a communalist.

speakers.name: Somnath Lahiri
speakers.positionSummary: Challenges the search of his house and seizure of Assembly-related papers and reminds the President of his Interim Government membership after the matter is referred for legal advice.

interventions.summary: The President declares H. C. Mookherjee the only validly nominated candidate and therefore duly elected Vice-President, then calls Pattabhi Sitaramayya to move the next resolution.

Pattabhi Sitaramayya moves a three-member Business Committee—Gopalaswami Ayyangar, K. M. Munshi and Biswanath Das—to recommend the order of future constitution-making business before the next preliminary session.
B. Gopala Reddy seconds the Business Committee resolution.
Satyanarayan Sinha moves a minimum two-member quorum for the Business Committee. Pattabhi accepts it and the amended resolution is adopted.

Rajagopalachari moves a committee to examine the scope of subjects assigned to the Union Centre, originally proposing twelve elected members plus up to ten presidential additions and an April reporting deadline.

Gibbon questions how the mover can discuss amendments before they are formally moved. The Chair allows Rajagopalachari to explain the anticipated amended structure without treating it as already incorporated.

Rajagopalachari explains the proposed membership and argues that Union finance, provincial and group constitutions, residual powers, and later incorporation of Advisory Committee recommendations create coordination problems that require advance constitutional thinking.

He rejects the idea that the Assembly is merely registering prior agreements, urges serious independent constitutional thought, and says absent League members should not be misunderstood even while work proceeds.
interventions.excerpt: We have to do a lot of substantial thinking

interventions.summary: With the Chair's permission, Satyanarayan Sinha moves Munshi's amendments: a named twelve-member initial committee, presidential filling of casual vacancies and a one-third quorum.
Gibbon questions whether someone else may move Munshi's amendments in Munshi's absence. The Chair permits it.
P. R. Thakur asks the committee to consider whether the Centre should have responsibilities capable of addressing communal disturbance and famine, citing Bengal's experience.

Jaipal Singh accepts the eminence of the proposed members but says the list looks like a plan for uniformity rather than unity. He asks why tribal areas and figures such as Jayakar, Ambedkar and Deshmukh are absent.
interventions.excerpt: the plan is not for unity but for uniformity

interventions.summary: Harnam Singh replies that the committee is technical and exploratory rather than a final allocation body, so members should prioritise constitutional expertise over communal or tribal representation.
N. G. Ranga asks one proposed member to withdraw so B. R. Ambedkar can be included.
Rajagopalachari defends the list as containing experienced constitutional thinkers and says the President's additional nominations can later address Muslim League, princely State and other omissions.
An unnamed member asks about Ranga's amendment; the Chair clarifies that Ranga made a suggestion rather than moving an amendment, then the amended Union-subject resolution is adopted.

Satyanarayan Sinha moves that the preliminary meeting stand adjourned to a day in April to be fixed by the President, anticipating the Business Committee and Union Committee reports at the next meeting.

Santhanam argues that a long adjournment should specify a particular date. The Chair reads Rule 21 differently, saying House consent is required for more than three days but the date itself may be fixed later.
Mohan Lal Saksena seconds the adjournment motion.
Seth Govind Das initially questions whether a resolution is needed at all; the Chair explains that Rule 21 requires the House's consent for an adjournment longer than three days.
Kamath argues that repeated postponement cannot continue merely because members remain absent and moves to state that no further adjournment of the preliminary meeting should occur after April.
Gopalaswami Ayyangar supports Santhanam's interpretation that the President must fix a date and that House consent only permits that date to lie beyond three days. The Chair maintains his ruling.
Rajagopalachari argues that once the House grants leave to adjourn beyond three days, the President can later fix any suitable date beyond that period.
Govind Das says changing conditions may require another adjournment and opposes binding the future Assembly in advance.
Satyanarayan asks Kamath to withdraw. Kamath does so, and the House adopts the original adjournment motion.
With listed business complete, Rajendra Prasad opens a short round of congratulations to H. C. Mookherjee and offers his own first.
Jerome D'Souza praises Mookherjee's cross-community esteem, educational record and expected fairness if called to preside.
Biswanath Das presents Mookherjee's election as evidence that minorities need not fear majority communities and as an honour to Bengal.
H. J. Khandekar offers congratulations on behalf of the Scheduled Caste community he represents.
Joseph Alban D'Souza connects Mookherjee's election to Indian Christian participation and hopes he will support the community's work through the Advisory Committee.

Mookherjee recounts his movement from communal politics to nationalism after seeing that poor Christians shared the same material condition as poor Hindus and Muslims. He promises to remember the poor masses rather than act as a communalist.
interventions.excerpt: from a Communalist I became a nationalist

interventions.summary: Kamath asks the President to address Somnath Lahiri's complaint that police searched his house and seized papers related to Assembly proceedings and speech notes. Harnam Singh raises a point of order because the adjournment motion has already passed; the Chair nevertheless permits the factual issue to be placed on record.
Rajendra Prasad says he referred Lahiri's letter to the Constitutional Adviser because it raises a legal question and will decide what action, if any, is available after studying the advice.
Lahiri reminds Rajendra Prasad that he is also a member of the Interim Government. The President sharply separates the roles inside the chamber.
interventions.excerpt: In this House, I am nothing else.

interventions.summary: The President adjourns the Assembly to a date in April to be fixed later, ending the January session.
